nextStep: Continue current native runtime editing/cancellation/restart/cache-corruption qualification and inspect warm-restore waiting cost before adoption.
limitations: New production progressive workload supplements the unchanged original direct-package four-load persistence benchmark; neither substitutes for the other.
Explicit maxFiles equals fixture size. Full project readiness and cache hits are checked; progressive intentionally excludes dependencies and reports complete=false.

Actual server Linux wait4 high water includes builtin initialization, real worker threads, all queries and shutdown. Fixture generation/driver RSS and simultaneous independent-process totals are not included.
First protocol completion is observed without query/index prewarm; editor-visible first result is not measured.
The cold-index budget applies to actual server index start/end interval; startup-to-index and first exact response are separately reported. Warm restore has no separate original hard threshold.
Hot queries use 100 requests per method after full project readiness, distinct from the first pre-readiness requests.
No paired comparison with historical normal runs or five-round direct-package statistics is implied.
Other modes/platforms/PHP versions, provider/tool combinations, corruption/cancellation/long sessions and human WSL remain open.
Normal Controller 157.74/150 ms and normal complete 10k 920.54/768 MiB are not closed by isolated candidate results; full C1-C4/R4 and P0-P9/F01-F14 remain active.
